title: When He opens a door
hookLine: when He opens a door of knowing Him, don't mind how little your deeds are (Hikam 8, paraphrased)
tomorrow: the reed has been crying since page one. what's it saying now?

cards: An email says you've been invited. A coach waves you up to the varsity bench. A friend's mother opens the door and says, come in, sit, eat.
And sometimes the first feeling isn't joy at all. It's: they've made a mistake. My grades, my record, my prayer habits don't match this door.
Should you walk in anyway? Ibn Ata'illah has a sentence for that exact flinch, and today it gets something you can feel in your feet: a doorway.

teach.b: Saying eight of the Hikam, paraphrased: when He opens a door for you to know Him, don't worry that your deeds are few. He opened it only because He wanted to make Himself known to you.
Don't you see that the knowing is His gift to you, while your deeds are your gift to Him? And how far apart those two gifts are. Read it slowly and the flinch falls apart.
The door was never measured against your record. It was measured against the giver. Your deeds still matter; they're what you carry in.
They're just not the key. Now the threshold itself.
Sahih Muslim keeps a short prayer for walking into a masjid: O God, open for me the doors of Your mercy. The custom is to step in right foot first, saying those words on the way.
Every visit to a masjid starts by standing in a doorway and asking for one to open. On the way out, there's a matching line asking for His bounty.

teach.h: A SMALL STEP, A LARGE ROOM.
teach.b: So the threshold is a lesson you can feel underfoot: the step in is small, and what it opens onto is large. That's the whole saying. Don't stand outside the open door counting your deeds.

how: Muslims enter a masjid right foot first and say, following Sahih Muslim, 'O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy'; leaving, they step out left foot first and ask for His bounty.

games.q: what does “when he opens a door” mean?
o: an opening to know God that your deeds didn't earn
a sign that your worship is finally good enough
a reward God gives for a long list of good works

games.q: what's inside the day — tap the pairs.
p: open for me the doors of Your mercy
measured by the giver, not your record

s: you should feel worthy before you accept an opening toward God
Hikam 8: don't mind how few your deeds are. He opened it because He wanted to be known.
Sahih Muslim keeps a prayer for entering a masjid: open for me the doors of Your mercy
every visit begins at a threshold, asking for a door to open.
Ibn Ata'illah says deeds don't matter at all
they still matter; they're what you carry in. they're just not the key.

games.q: a neighbor at the masjid invites you to the weekly Qur'an circle. you can barely read Arabic and everyone else seems fluent. what fits Hikam 8?
o: go. the door was opened for you, not for your reading level.
wait a year until your Arabic is good enough to keep up.
go, but keep quiet so nobody notices how little you know.
games.why: the door is measured by the giver, not your record. walk through, and bring what you have.

practice: Stand up and walk slowly to the nearest doorway. Pause at the threshold for one full breath, then step through and take a few unhurried steps on the other side, feeling each foot land.
Some Muslims step into a masjid right foot first, asking God to open the doors of His mercy; carry that line through with you, or just the step.

wordCard.voice: When He opens a door: Ibn Ata'illah's eighth saying. The knowing is His gift to you; your deeds are your gift to Him.

orig.note: Arabic: door, gate; its plural is in the prayer for entering a masjid, 'the doors of Your mercy.'

carryVoice: One line for the threshold: walk through, and let the giver worry about the size of the door. Six sayings, and the Hikam is done.

sources.ref: Ibn Ata'illah al-Iskandari, al-Hikam, aphorism 8 (when He opens a door of knowing, don't mind how few your deeds are)
Sahih Muslim 713 (on entering the mosque: open for me the doors of Your mercy; on leaving: I ask You of Your bounty)
